expl: 19(1)(b) assembly vs 19(3) public-order/sovereignty limits; any curb must be reasonable — narrow, time-bound, route-specific, reasoned (BNSS order). Blanket indefinite bans fail Maneka fairness too.
options: Ban all processions indefinitely without reasons
Impose a narrow time-bound route-specific order with recorded reasons
No restriction is ever allowed on processions
q: A week after a communal clash, a procession is planned. Lawful course?
trapnote: Blanket-ban overreach vs no-restriction absolutism — reasonableness is the middle tested.

why.0: Wrong: blanket + indefinite + unreasoned fails 19(3) reasonableness.
why.1: Correct: restriction on a listed ground, proportionate and recorded.
why.3: Wrong: arrest needs offence + procedure, not mere apprehension.

expl: Illegal custody = Habeas Corpus: Art. 32 (needs State respondent) or Art. 226 (any person/authority, wider). Missing youth in unofficial custody fits directly; Zee Telefilms logic shows forum choice matters.
options: File habeas corpus — Art. 32 if State custody, Art. 226 reaches even private hands
Only a missing-person diary, no writ
Habeas corpus lies only during Emergency
q: A youth is held in unofficial custody beyond 24 hours without record. Family seeks immediate production. Advise?
trapnote: Diary-only understates remedy; Emergency-only inverts habeas (strongest in normalcy).

why.0: Correct: produce-the-body writ with forum chosen by who detains.
why.1: Wrong: diary does not produce the body.
why.2: Wrong: damages later don't end illegal custody now.
why.3: Wrong: habeas is routine; Emergency was when it was denied (ADM Jabalpur).

expl: Mandamus (we command) compels public duty: eligible licence + refusal = textbook case. Not Prohibition (pre-judgment court excess), Certiorari (quash passed order) or Quo-Warranto (office title).
options: Mandamus to perform the public duty
q: An officer refuses a licence though every condition is met. Correct writ?
trapnote: Writ-function confusion: each wrong option belongs to a different defect.

why.0: Wrong: no court exceeding jurisdiction here.
why.1: Wrong: no passed order to quash.
why.3: Wrong: applicant holds no office to challenge.

expl: Quo-Warranto (by what authority) tests illegal occupation of public office — qualification defect fits. Habeas (custody), Mandamus (duty), Prohibition (pre-judgment excess) do not.
q: An unqualified person sits on a statutory public board. Correct writ?
trapnote: Office-title vs order-merits vs custody confusion across writs.

why.1: Correct: challenges the holder's title to office.
why.3: Wrong: no court proceeding to restrain.

expl: Royappa: transfer to same-pay side post with zero recorded reason is pleadable arbitrariness under Art. 14 — no group comparison needed. Maneka extends to unfair procedure; courts test absence of reason itself.
options: No Art. 14 case without a comparison group
Arbitrariness plea under Art. 14 without group comparison
q: An officer is shifted to a same-pay side post with nothing on file. Art. 14 plea?
trapnote: No-group-no-case is pre-Royappa law; pay-cut-only invents a condition.

why.0: Wrong: Royappa removed the group requirement.
why.1: Wrong: constitutional review overlays service law.
why.2: Wrong: status/reason, not pay, is the test.

expl: 22(2): elapsed 39 hrs (8 pm Mon-11 am Wed) minus 11 hrs journey = 28 hrs, still beyond 24. Violation stands. Exclusion belongs to punitive arrest; preventive track has no 24-hr rule at all.
options: No violation since journey is excluded
Violation because journey exclusion is only for preventive detention
No rule since 24 hours is only BNSS, not Constitution
q: Arrest 8 pm Monday, 300 km away, produced 11 am Wednesday; journey took 11 hours. Art. 22(2)?
trapnote: Recognise-rule-then-stop-thinking (skip subtraction); inverted track for the exclusion.

why.0: Wrong: subtraction first — exclusion does not save 28 hours.
why.2: Wrong: exclusion is punitive-track; preventive has no 24-hr rule.
why.3: Wrong: rule is both constitutional (22(2)) and statutory.

expl: 39A (free legal aid) is DPSP, non-justiciable alone; read with Art. 21 it becomes enforceable (Hussainara/Khatri) via Legal Services Authorities Act + BNSS aid provisions. Produce + inform + aid.
options: Produce, inform of aid, connect to legal services (39A read with Art. 21)
Remand without counsel since DPSP is unenforceable
Deny aid as a non-citizen issue
q: An indigent labourer with no lawyer is produced for remand. Duty?
trapnote: DPSP-alone-enforces and DPSP-never-matters are opposite errors; citizenship irrelevant.

expl: Art. 25(2)(b) empowers throwing open Hindu public institutions; 2018 4:1 struck the bar (not denomination, not essential; Malhotra dissented) but 14 Nov 2019 referred larger questions to nine judges (2026 hearings live) — never quote 2018 as final.
options: Custom alone decides, courts cannot look
Only Art. 26 protects the custom fully
2018 (4:1) plus pending nine-judge reference — not settled law
q: A temple bars women 10-50 by custom; legality is questioned. Exam-safe answer?
trapnote: Settled-law vs courts-can-never-look are opposite absolutes on evolving law.

why.1: Wrong: denomination claim failed the 2018 test.

expl: Art. 30 needs established AND administered by the minority (TMA Pai, State unit); State may regulate excellence but not destroy character; Art. 15(5) (93rd) expressly excepts Art. 30 institutions from private-college quota.
options: Minority institutions must take State quota like others
Aid denial on minority ground violates Art. 30; 15(5) quota skips minorities
Minorities need only administer, not establish
q: A minority school is denied aid for its minority character while a quota is forced on it. Position?
trapnote: Only-administer drops a limb; no-qualification-check denies lawful regulation.

expl: PESA (1996, under 243M(4)(b), Bhuria): Gram Sabha supreme — minor-mineral leases need its recommendation; AP Scheduled Areas include ASR, Parvathipuram Manyam, Eluru. Obstruction may assert statutory right — verify resolution before registering.
options: Verify Gram Sabha resolution first — PESA right may cover them
q: A contractor with a State minor-mineral permit faces village obstruction in a Scheduled Area. First step?
trapnote: Obstruction-first policing without checking the PESA right risks acting against statute.

why.1: Wrong: permit may be genuine yet insufficient without Sabha.
why.2: Wrong: preventive detention inapplicable to rights assertion.
why.3: Correct: Sabha recommendation is the gating requirement.

expl: Art. 371D (32nd Amend, Six-Point Formula) empowers the President by ORDER to organise local cadres/areas/recruitment (1975 Order); survives 2014 for AP + Telangana. Distinct from 16(3) Parliament-by-law residence rule.
options: 371D Presidential Order local cadres — valid zonal posting
q: An SI is posted zone-wise, challenging it as anti-merit. Reply?
trapnote: 371D-as-16(3) merger and ended-in-2014 both misstate instrument and survival.

why.0: Correct: Order-based local cadres, living law in both States.
why.2: Wrong: 16(3) is Parliament-law residence, different route.

expl: Epuru Sudhakar (2006, AP): clemency reviewable on limited grounds — no application of mind, mala fide, irrelevant/extraneous grounds, suppressed/ignored facts; on ministerial advice; 72 pardons death + martial, 161 neither.
options: Only the President's orders are reviewable
Reviewable limitedly: mala fide, irrelevant grounds, no mind, wrong facts
Governor acts on personal discretion alone
q: A Governor remits a political killer citing good political worker on wrong facts. Challenge?
trapnote: Fully-beyond-courts predates 2006; personal-discretion denies ministerial advice.

why.0: Wrong: Epuru Sudhakar opened limited review.
why.1: Wrong: 72 and 161 both reviewable on same grounds.
why.3: Wrong: power runs on Council advice.

expl: Puttaswamy (2017, 9 judges): privacy inside Art. 21; limits need law + legitimate aim + proportionality. Phone/laptop opening, tapping, biometrics, CCTV need legal base. No cited law = violation.
options: Allowed: quick checks need no law
Violates Puttaswamy: no legal basis cited
q: An officer opens a suspect's phone for a quick look, citing no law. Position?
trapnote: Quick-check pragmatism vs Aadhaar-only narrowing both dodge the legality limb.

why.0: Wrong: legality is limb one of three.
why.1: Correct: no law = fails at the first step.
why.2: Wrong: speech freedom is not device-search power.
why.3: Wrong: privacy covers device contents generally.
